label: prf:crossed-module-euler-characteristic
title: Proof of crossed module euler characteristic
html:
Proof. The Borromean braid has 6 crossings with quaternion images [i, -j, i, -j, i, -j] and signs [+1, -1, +1, -1, +1, -1]. The \binom{6}{2} = 15 pairwise products s_k s_l \, c_k c_l are 2 \times 2 quaternion matrices. Their sum has trace:

  \mathrm{tr}\!\bigl(\textstyle\sum_{k < l}
  s_k s_l \, c_k c_l\bigr)
  = \mathrm{tr}\!\begin{pmatrix}
    -6 & 3i \\ 3i & -6
  \end{pmatrix}
  = -12.

Since \dim(V) = 2 and \chi(\Sigma_4) = 2 - 2 \cdot 4 = -6, the identity -12 = 2 \cdot (-6) holds. \square

The complete non-abelian Stokes chain connecting the three layers:

Layer Value Source
Algebraic (Q_{8} crossed module) -12 \dim(V) \cdot \chi(\Sigma_4)
Geometric (hyperbolic volume) -8G -12 \times \tfrac{2G}{3} (Bring bridge)
Boundary (Markov trace \kappa) \tfrac{3}{16} -12 \div (-64) via \Phi_0

The Bring bridge factor \tfrac{2G}{3} = \tfrac{4}{3}\,\Lambda(\pi/4) converts the algebraic per-cell curvature -\tfrac{3}{2} to the geometric per-cell volume -G (Catalan constant), where \Lambda is the Lobachevsky function and G = \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)/8.
